card.name: Subject word before 'take' or 'taking'
card.fires_on: The subject word (it, may, patients) right before a verb like take, taking or require, often in sentences about how long something takes. It appears in dosing and time-to-effect text.

modes.label: Dummy 'it' or 'may' before 'take'
modes.description: The word it or may sits just before a phrase about duration, such as may take longer or it may take up to 2 years.
modes.example: Without use of an accelerated drug elimination procedure, it<< may>> take up to 2 years to reach

modes.label: Patients before 'taking'
modes.description: The word patients comes right before taking a named drug.
modes.example: 2.5 Dosing in Patients Taking Valproate<< Patients>> taking valproate should begin ruf

card.plain: It fires on the word just before a likely 'take' or 'taking', such as 'it may take up to 24 hours'.
